test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 09 May 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Working 15 hours a day, Vaibhav can complete a piece of work in 35 days. How many hours a day should he work so as finish the work in 25 days?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = 35 × 15 = 525 hours

Required hours per day = Total work ÷ New number of days

Required hours per day = 525 ÷ 25 = 21 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 21 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Vaibhav (Case 1)
 35
 175
 175 ÷ 35 = 5
 
 

 Vaibhav (Case 2)
 25
 175 ÷ 25 = 7
 
 

⇒ In Case 1, Vaibhav works 15 hours per day to achieve a daily efficiency of 5 units.

⇒ Work done per hour = 5 ÷ 15 = 1/3 units/hour

⇒ In Case 2, Vaibhav's required daily efficiency is 7 units.

⇒ Number of hours required per day = Required daily efficiency ÷ Work done per hour

⇒ Hours per day = 7 ÷ (1/3)

⇒ Hours per day = 7 × 3 = 21 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 21 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Formula)

The general formula for time and work is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

When the total work remains constant, the number of days taken is inversely proportional to the number of hours worked per day (i.e., more hours per day means fewer days required).
